item.title: Meta settles in US states lawsuit on teen user addiction
item.description: Meta has agreed to pay what could amount to billions of dollars and to implement platform usage limitations on young users in a lawsuit brought by US states. The challenge revolved around addiction issues and overuse.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
item.description: An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Zambia after the polls: A test for democracy in Africa
item.description: Zambia's democratic institutions are under scrutiny, as the opposition continues to dispute the election results and courts remain closed. Weeks after the election, Zambia’s election story might be far from over.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India: Assam tea industry faces climate-driven labor crisis
item.description: Plantations in Assam produce more than half of India's tea. But rising heat is hurting yields, workers are increasingly leaving for more stable work, and producers are feeling the squeeze of stagnant tea prices.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Grain exports stall as Ukraine steps up attacks on Russia's Black Sea ports
item.description: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian infrastructure on the Black Sea are disrupting grain and oil exports from the port of Novorossiysk and other key hubs.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Houthi strikes threaten to pull Yemen back into full-scale war
item.description: The Iran-backed Houthis are using regional warfare to increase pressure on Saudi Arabia, while their attacks risk reopening Yemen's own conflict and disrupting shipping in the Red Sea.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nigeria's jet fuel conundrum: Scarcity at home, abundance abroad
item.description: Nigeria is fast becoming Europe's biggest jet fuel supplier, as it continues to help ease ongoing shortages abroad. Meanwhile at home, the West African country’s own airlines are struggling to keep their tanks full.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Will Iran withdraw from nuclear non-proliferation treaty?
item.description: Iranian lawmakers have again raised the possibility of leaving a decades-old international nuclear weapons treaty. Analysts say the threat to quit may offer Tehran more leverage than an actual withdrawal.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Starlink won't open Vietnam's heavily censored internet
item.description: Starlink promises better connectivity in remote and mountainous areas. But in one of Southeast Asia's most tightly controlled online environments, more network access doesn't mean more free speech.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
item.description: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: US: Trump administration plans to revoke up to 200,000 visas from asylum seekers
item.description: The State Department is reportedly looking to revoke the visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who sought asylum after entering on tourist or business visas, in what could be the largest mass visa revocation in US history.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: DR Congo peace roadmap: Will the fighting finally end?
item.description: A new roadmap sets out the conditions toward peace in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). But disagreements over M23 rebels, Rwanda's role and security concerns remain, and could still derail the process.
item.dc:subject: World
